hero.kicker: For veterans, widows and widowers outside the US
hero.h1: Getting in to VA.gov, ID.me and Social Security from abroad
hero.lede: Signing in from another country breaks in many places: a code that never arrives, a document refused, a video call in the middle of the night, a password that belonged to someone who has died. This page lists each place it breaks and the way through, the routes that need no login at all, and how to tell a helper from a scammer.

before.intro: ID.me checks your identity in two sittings: first you upload documents; once they are approved, usually within a day, you can book a video call with an agent in the US. Having everything below ready saves a third and fourth sitting.

items: Your passport, not expired. A passport from any country can count.
A bank statement or electricity bill less than a year old, showing your current address.
Your US Social Security number (SSN), if you have one.
For a widow or widower: the marriage certificate and the death certificate.
The veteran's DD214 (discharge paper) and VA file number, if you have them.
An English translation of every document not in English.
Your own number, not the late spouse's, able to receive text messages.
Charged, connected to wifi, with automatic screen lock turned off.
A front camera that works.
iPhone: Settings > Camera > Formats > Most Compatible, and Live Photos off. Other photo formats are refused.
An email address that is yours, that you can open today, with its password written down.
Your name spelled the same way on every document, or a list of every spelling.
Dates on Thai documents in the Buddhist Era (2510) written with the Western year beside them (1967).
Your address typed exactly as the bank statement prints it, letter for letter.

before.two: Plan two sittings from the start. Sitting one: account, security codes, documents. Sitting two: the video call, then back to VA.gov to press Allow.

items: Before anything else, write down what is needed from old phones and computers: email addresses, passwords, phone numbers. Old devices often cannot open ID.me.
Do the reading and typing on a current device. The photos of documents and the selfie work best from the person's own phone.
Turn off any VPN. ID.me blocks many of them (error 1015).
Translate each screen aloud. ID.me is in English and Spanish; a Thai or other interpreter is available only once the video call starts.
The person can ask for an interpreter on the video call, and a family member or helper may sit beside them. A power of attorney cannot speak for them on the call.
Keep a note of where it stopped and why, so the next sitting starts there.

credentials.intro: VA.gov accepts three sign-ins. DS Logon ended on 18 November 2025 and My HealtheVet sign-in on 5 March 2025.

rows.name: ID.me
rows.abroad: Yes, through its overseas route and a video call.
rows.needs: A passport and proof of address. A non-US passport can count.

rows.name: Login.gov
rows.abroad: Hard. It refuses non-US passports and IDs and international phone numbers. In-person checks are at US Post Offices only.
rows.needs: A US ID or US passport, an SSN, a US phone number or a letter by post.

credentials.note: Login.gov lists international users among its plans for 2027. Until then, ID.me is the route for most people outside the US.

idme.h: ID.me from abroad, step by step

steps.body: Go to VA.gov, choose Sign in, then ID.me. Create the account with your own email address.
Set up two ways to get codes: text message to your number, and the ID.me Authenticator app or a passkey. If texts do not arrive, the app still works.

ID.me shows two large buttons, Self-Service and Video Call, and a smaller link, "I don't live in the United States" or "I don't have the above documents". The small link is the overseas route. The two large buttons expect US documents.
Choose your country under current address. Enter your SSN if you have one.

Two primary documents, or one primary and one secondary. A passport is primary; a bank statement or electricity bill is secondary. A document not in English goes side by side with its English translation, in the same photo. ID.me can text you a link to take the photos with your phone.
Usually within 24 hours, by email. A rejection email is titled "Action Required: Update your document(s)" and has a button to send them again.
Calls can be booked up to 10 days ahead, and from 2 hours ahead on the same day. Times show in your local time. Booking avoids waiting in a queue; leaving the queue puts you at the back.

Have the original documents in your hand; copies and photos are refused, and a document written on is refused. An interpreter in your language is available on request. The agent confirms your name, date of birth, address and SSN.
Open a new tab, go to VA.gov, sign in with ID.me again, and press Allow. Pressing Deny limits what VA.gov can show you.

idme.nossn: ID.me has a route for a non-US passport with no SSN: the passport, proof of the same address, and a box confirming no SSN or ITIN was ever issued. VA.gov's own page says that without an SSN you need a US passport. Which rule VA.gov applies to a widow or widower with a foreign passport is not settled on either site. If you try it, keep a screenshot of each screen.

wrong.intro: What you see, what is happening, and the way through.

items.q: The code by text message never arrives.
items.a: Texts to some countries arrive late or not at all. Press Resend, then Call me. A second method set up in advance, the ID.me Authenticator app or a passkey, works without text messages.

items.q: "We couldn't verify your browser" or "Something isn't right".
items.a: The browser is too old, or JavaScript is off. Use a current Chrome, Safari, Edge or Firefox with no extensions.
A VPN or proxy is on. Turn it off and try again.
iPhone photos in HEIC format and Live Photos are refused. Settings > Camera > Formats > Most Compatible.
A document not in English has to be photographed beside its English translation, both in one picture.

items.q: The name on one document does not match another.
items.a: Names from Thai, Lao, Khmer, Korean, Chinese and other scripts are spelled in English in different ways on different papers. Bring every document that shows the name, and a translation that follows the passport spelling.
A bank and a utility company may spell the same address differently in English. Type the address exactly as the document you upload prints it.
Thai documents count years in the Buddhist Era, 543 years ahead: 2510 is 1967. A translation can give both.
Each person can have one verified ID.me account. The message may show only initials and the end of an email address. That clue tells you which old email address holds the account.

items.q: The video call queue is hours long.
items.a: The agents are in the US. Book a time instead of queueing; booking opens once documents are approved.

items.q: The phone went to sleep and the call ended.
items.a: Turn off automatic screen lock, plug in the charger, stay on wifi, and book again.
Copies, photos of documents, expired passports, temporary IDs and documents with writing on them are refused. Glare and creases can also fail. Originals, flat, in good light.

items.q: After ID.me, VA.gov shows an error.
items.a: The VA.gov session timed out while you were away. Close the tab, open a new one, sign in again and press Allow.
A new number means resetting security codes in ID.me, and sometimes a longer video call to confirm it is you.

items.q: There is no one to phone at ID.me.
items.a: ID.me support is by chat and an online form, in English and Spanish. Chat is fastest, with the person present.

items.q: Messages from ID.me look like a scammer's.
items.a: ID.me sends codes and links by text and email in English. Expect them during the sittings; a message you did not ask for, from someone wanting a code read back, is the scammer's.

items.q: Login.gov or CLEAR will not accept you.
items.a: Both need a US Social Security number, and Login.gov needs US documents. ID.me is the route from abroad.

items.q: You do not know how many tries are left.
items.a: ID.me does not publish a limit. After two failures at the same step, the video call route is the next step.
Most claims can be made on paper by post or fax, with no login. See below.

death.intro: For a widow or widower. Each step has a paper route below.

items.h: His or her account is not yours
items.body: A veteran's ID.me and VA.gov accounts are tied to the veteran's identity, and security codes go to the veteran's phone and email. VA takes back payments made after the death. A surviving spouse needs an account of their own, or the paper route.

To VA, by phone or by post to the Claims Intake Center. To Social Security, through the Federal Benefits Unit for your country or the international call center. For a US citizen, also to the nearest US embassy or consulate, which can issue a Consular Report of Death Abroad.

Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC), Survivors Pension and accrued benefits all use VA Form 21P-534EZ. Filed within one year of the death, payment can start from the first day of the month of the death.
For the surviving spouse of a veteran who was rated permanently and totally disabled, or who died of a service-connected condition. VA Form 10-10d.

Through the Federal Benefits Unit. A one-time payment of $255 goes to a surviving spouse. Outside the US, a survivor who is not a US citizen usually needs five years of US residence in the marriage; that rule does not apply when the veteran died in military service or of a service-connected condition.
VA Form 21-0845 lets VA speak with a person you name. VA Form 21-22 appoints a veterans service organization (VSO) to act for you, free.

paper.h: No login: by post, fax and phone
paper.intro: Send by tracked post or fax, and keep a copy of every page and the receipt.

labels.check: From an older page; not confirmed on a current one.

dic.note: Within one year of the death, payment can start from the first of that month. Whether Survivors Pension is paid to someone living in your country is a question for VA before you post the packet.

death_va.note: Post is slower to stop payments than a call.

death_ssa.h: Report a death to Social Security, and survivor benefits
death_ssa.note: Thailand and several other Asian countries are served from Manila. Other countries: ssa.gov/foreign lists each Federal Benefits Unit.

fmp.h: Foreign Medical Program (the veteran's own service-connected care)
fmp.note: Covers the veteran only, not the spouse.

helpers.note: VA's pages give no postal address for these forms from abroad; the Claims Intake Center is the likely one.

lines.va_abroad: VA benefits, from outside the US
lines.vcl: Veterans Crisis Line, Asia and the Pacific

items: A VA-accredited veterans service organization (VSO) helps with claims for free.
VA-accredited attorneys and claims agents may charge only after VA has decided the first claim, with a signed fee agreement and VA Form 21-22a on file.
Anyone's accreditation can be checked on VA's search: va.gov/get-help-from-accredited-representative/find-rep
In Thailand, American Legion Post TH01 is in Ubon Ratchathani and Post TH02 in Pattaya.

scammers.intro: Veterans, widows and widowers are offered "help" by people who take the claim, the payments or the savings. Being scammed is not your fault; careful people are scammed too. The sooner someone you trust knows, the more can be saved.
signs: They contacted you first, by phone, LINE, WhatsApp or Facebook, often after a funeral.
They want money before filing, or a share of the back pay.
They promise the money, or more of it.
They ask for a password, or the code you were just texted.
They rush you: today, or you lose it.
They say to keep it from your family.
They want the bank account for VA or Social Security payments changed.
They want payment to a personal account, in gift cards, or in crypto.
They want savings moved into insurance, an annuity or a fund so you "qualify" for a pension.
They say they are VA or ID.me, from a personal LINE, WhatsApp or Gmail account.
Their name is not in VA's accreditation search.
A link to an ID.me video call arrives that you did not book.
do: Stop: hang up, no links, no codes, no transfers.
Keep proof: screenshots of the chat, the phone number, the account name, any bank account they gave.
Money already sent: call your bank at once, then the police. In Thailand, call 1441 first, any hour: it can ask banks to halt a transfer.
ID.me password or code given away: change the password and the security-code method, then use ID.me's Report Suspicious Activity form.
VA payments sent to a new account: call VA's international direct deposit line.
Fraud against VA benefits: VA Inspector General hotline.
Someone not accredited charged for claim help: a complaint to VA's Office of General Counsel.

items: 1441: the Anti Online Scam Operation Center (AOC), 24 hours. It can ask banks to halt a transfer; a police report at thaipoliceonline.go.th or a station completes it.
1323: Department of Mental Health, free, 24 hours, Thai.
1669: medical emergency.
Social Security for Thailand: Federal Benefits Unit at the US Embassy in Manila.
Translations of Thai documents: Chiang Mai Visa Desk.

care.intro: Grief, money worries, being scammed, hours of failed sign-ins: it is a lot. Talking to someone helps.
items: Veterans Crisis Line, from anywhere: chat at veteranscrisisline.net/get-help-now/chat
From Asia and the Pacific by phone: +1 844 702 5493 (international charges apply).
Thailand: 1323, free, 24 hours.
Other countries: findahelpline.com lists free lines by country.

bots.body: This page is a free guide for US veterans and surviving spouses living outside the United States who need to sign in to VA.gov, ID.me or Social Security, or claim without signing in. It is published in twelve languages, each with a plain text version. Facts were checked against VA, ID.me, Login.gov and Social Security pages on 20 October 2026; each source is linked. Quoting and linking are welcome.
